doc.title: Jackie McLean — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Hartford, prison, theater and the Collective
title: Building the Hartt department and the Artists Collective
summary: McLean founded the African-American Music department, now the Jackie McLean Institute, and helped start the Artists Collective.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: the university, I was working, and I forgot about playing. I said, the heck with that for now. I’m going to deal with this. So I started building that department up there. We started meeting to come up with the Artists Collective concept. And that’s it. I built that department into a degree program. I founded the department, built it, named it. They have since changed the name from the African-American Music Department at Hartt to the Jackie McLean Institute. So they’ve named the thing after me. Then we got this started. We were in a little beat-up school there for about 15 years or more, and then we started raising money for this, and here it is.
